rationale_evidence.anchor: Can two independent engineers implement the same kernel from the current material, without the research corpus? STILL NO. But the reason changed, and the change is the finding: [table of 5 blockers, 2026-08-31 vs 2026-09-02] The blockers moved DOWNWARD -- from vocabulary disagreement to semantic undefinedness. A vocabulary blocker is resolved by a governance act; a semantic blocker is resolved by a derivation. The estate has traded four governance blockers for four derivation blockers.
rationale_evidence.statement: Restates the central implementability readiness question (can two independent engineers implement the same kernel from current material without the research corpus?) as STILL NO, but frames the change as progress: five specific blockers are named across the 2026-08-31 and 2026-09-02 snapshots, and the overall shift is that blockers moved from vocabulary disagreement (resolvable by a governance act) to semantic undefinedness (resolvable only by a derivation) -- summarized as 'the estate has traded four governance blockers for four derivation blockers', explicitly framed as real progress since derivation blockers are the kind a research lane can actually discharge.

rationale_evidence.anchor: What is the single most important blocker? BLOCKER 1 -- which K is canonical. Not O_core, which is where every lane currently points. Reasons: 1. O_core is already in flight... 2. O_core is downstream of I, which is downstream of knowing which K the invariants range over... 3. Blocker 1 is the only one no derivation can resolve... 4. It gates 16 of 25 constructs at the Architecture lane simultaneously. Runner-up, and the one nobody has recorded: I -- the mandated invariant register. It is R_mandatory in the operation-necessity test AND the I in Sufficient(K,O,I). Two independent obligations, one missing object, no artifact noting they are the same.
rationale_evidence.statement: Names the single most important blocker as 'which K is canonical', explicitly NOT O_core (where every lane currently focuses), giving four reasons: O_core is already being worked; O_core is downstream of I, which is downstream of K, so working O_core first risks redoing it; Blocker 1 is the only blocker no derivation can resolve (only an authority can); it gates 16 of 25 architecture-lane constructs simultaneously. Names I (the invariant register) as the unrecorded runner-up blocker, observing it is simultaneously R_mandatory in the operation-necessity test and the I parameter in Sufficient(K,O,I) -- two independent obligations converging on one missing object, with no artifact anywhere noting they are the same thing.

rationale_evidence.anchor: The one-line finding: KnowledgeOS is not short of theory. It is short of one governance act, and the act has not been named: nobody has asked which K is canonical. Every lane is working on O_core. O_core is downstream of I, and I is downstream of K. The programme is optimising the third link of a chain whose first link is unattached.
rationale_evidence.statement: States the closing one-line finding of the whole readiness investigation: KnowledgeOS is not short of theory, it is short of one unasked governance act (which K is canonical); every research lane is currently working on O_core, which is downstream of I, which is downstream of K -- 'the programme is optimising the third link of a chain whose first link is unattached.'
